programme: MYB and ASCL2 maintain a progenitor/stem-cell identity program (ASCL2 is the canonical Wnt-driven intestinal stem cell master regulator; MYB sustains proliferative progenitor state), while SPDEF drives the opposing terminal step — secretory (goblet-type) differentiation. Together they form the stem-renewal-versus-secretory-differentiation axis that governs epithelial turnover in a crypt-like tissue.
role_in_a: In IBS-relevant colonic epithelium, this axis sets the balance between crypt progenitor renewal (MYB/ASCL2) and goblet-cell/mucin-producing differentiation (SPDEF); shifts in this balance track with the mucus-layer thinning, altered goblet-cell density and barrier changes reported in IBS mucosa.
role_in_b: In Kidney Papillary Cell Carcinoma, MYB carries an independently notable Open Targets signal (81st percentile of scored genes), consistent with a progenitor-identity program being genetically implicated in this tumor; if the same renewal-versus-differentiation logic operates in renal tubular epithelium, loss of a SPDEF-type terminal-differentiation step alongside MYB/ASCL2-driven progenitor persistence would fit the general dedifferentiation seen with higher tumor grade — but this specific axis is not documented for papillary RCC.
shared_axis: Both the intestinal crypt and the renal tubule are self-renewing epithelia that must balance progenitor maintenance against terminal secretory differentiation; the same MYB/ASCL2-versus-SPDEF logic recurring in each tissue would let a stalled or skewed differentiation step contribute to barrier/renewal dysfunction in IBS and to a dedifferentiated, progenitor-like tumor state in papillary RCC, without requiring the two diseases to share any documented pathway.
reasoning: The three factors form a genuinely nameable programme (stem/progenitor maintenance vs. secretory terminal differentiation), and MYB is independently placed in Kidney_Papillary_Cell_Carcinoma by a high Open Targets percentile, so this is not built on silence alone. But no retrieved source connects this specific axis, or ASCL2/SPDEF individually, to papillary RCC, and ASCL2's only retrieved paper addresses intestinal stem cells in general rather than IBS specifically — so the cross-disease bridge is inferential, not retrieved.
support: PMID 41576939 — links ASCL2 to intestinal stem cell function (general gut biology, not established for IBS specifically); no PMID places MYB or SPDEF in either disease — MYB's disease-B relevance rests only on its Open Targets percentile, not a citable paper.
how_to_falsify: Profile MYB, ASCL2 and SPDEF target-gene activity (or single-cell expression of progenitor vs. secretory/differentiation markers) in papillary RCC tumor tissue versus matched normal renal tubule; if higher-grade or more aggressive papillary RCC does not show relative gain of MYB/ASCL2 progenitor signature with loss of SPDEF-driven differentiation markers compared to normal tubule, this account is wrong.
caveats: Colorectal vs. kidney tissue pairing across 56 patient-group comparisons, but all of them fall under a single independent cohort pair — so the high recurrence counts reflect consistency across subgroups of one dataset, not replication across separate studies. SPDEF and ASCL2 have no Open Targets association in either disease, so the module rests mainly on MYB. FOXI1 and YBX1 (excluded from this account) do have literature support in kidney cancer, but FOXI1's papers describe chromophobe RCC/oncocytoma, not papillary RCC, and neither fits a differentiation-axis story with the other carrying factors. Seven single-view factors (NFKBIZ, BRCA1, MTA1, FOSL2, KLF5, FOXJ3, RLF) were correctly excluded as one-subgroup artifacts; no tissue-generic exclusion list was provided for this pair.
